roleTitle: Senior Product Manager - AI Competitive Intelligence

job.rawJd:
We're hiring a hands-on Senior Product Manager to lead an AI-driven competitive intelligence and conversational search platform that delivers deeper, more actionable insights than general-purpose AI chat products. The role owns product strategy and execution, from quarterly planning and metrics to features that extract data, create derivative datasets, and assemble them into a usable knowledge graph.

Responsibilities include owning the strategy and roadmap for an AI-driven, NLP-based competitive benchmarking product; leading data extraction and knowledge graph initiatives across company, people, event, and open-web data; delivering conversational search with embeddings and Boolean search; building SaaS AI capabilities with APIs and connectors; translating NLP, embeddings, knowledge graphs, LLM orchestration, and agentic workflows into customer value and go-to-market messaging; partnering with data science and engineering on data requirements, evaluation frameworks, and model strategy; conducting discovery with business users in financial and professional services; driving execution across engineering, data, design, and go-to-market teams; and supporting customer-facing conversations with sales and customer success.

First-90-day outcomes include ingesting and normalizing customer and market documents, generating derivative datasets and knowledge graph assets, improving data freshness through extraction and AI enrichment, launching conversational search with embeddings and Boolean search, defining a scalable AI model strategy and evaluation criteria, and setting metrics for adoption, answer quality, time-to-insight, data freshness, search effectiveness, and cost-performance.

Qualifications include 5-8+ years of product management experience with at least 3 years leading AI/ML, NLP, search, or knowledge graph products; commercial judgment; cross-functional leadership; hands-on familiarity with LLMs, embeddings, NLP, retrieval/search, and agentic workflows; quarterly planning and metric-driven product development; clear technical and customer communication; analytical problem solving; and relevant work in professional services, financial services, competitive intelligence, or market research. Nice-to-haves include vector or semantic search, conversational AI, knowledge graphs, NLP pipelines, AI data enrichment, and products that combine structured and unstructured data.

paragraphs: I am applying for the Senior Product Manager role with Confidential Employer because it brings together the parts of product work where I am strongest: finding the business question, shaping the AI workflow, and making a technical product useful to customers. My background spans current AI product implementation, enterprise marketing intelligence, UX research, and eight years of Fortune 500 client leadership.

Through One Block Away, I lead client discovery and turn unclear questions into working AI POCs, demo flows, and roadmap decisions. I built WeReady's Bailey Intelligence dashboard around founder inputs, GitHub signals, government and academic sources, source health, risk scoring, and evidence trails. The case study is clear that source-linked semantic search is the next layer, not a feature I have already shipped. At Hedgehox, I turn recurring agency problems into governed AI workflows for claims review, evidence gaps, scoping, routing, and regulatory monitoring.

Earlier, I led research and UX strategy for Kinesso's marketing intelligence suite, used by more than 7,000 people across 22 white-label brands. Interviews, prototype testing, beta groups, behavioral analytics, and adoption data became roadmap priorities across more than 20 products. I also led research and design for Kanvas, a developer-first API services library, partnering with product and engineering on the roadmap and with C-suite stakeholders on monetization and go-to-market planning.

I would bring direct product, customer, and commercial leadership from adjacent AI and intelligence products. I would not present my background as production ownership of embeddings, Boolean search, knowledge graphs, or data pipelines. The useful bridge is my experience defining the customer problem, organizing source-backed workflows, translating technical behavior into decisions, and working with engineering and data partners to move a product from idea to a testable release.
I would welcome a conversation about how that mix could help the team build a competitive-intelligence product customers can trust and use.
